fields.meta_title: NFT Landing Page Builder for Your Drop | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an NFT landing page from a prompt. See four examples: an allowlist form, mint reminders, a jacket redemption, and signups by link.
fields.h1: Build an NFT Landing Page for Your Next Drop
fields.hero_description: Get an NFT landing page built from one prompt, with an allowlist form and every signup saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Everything a Drop Page Needs, From One Prompt
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the collection page and the signup form under it, plus the table that holds every collector who signs up.
fields.feature_1:
The page, written from one sentence

Describe the collection and the drop date, plus the one thing a visitor should do. Emergent builds the page around the artwork and its signup form, and another prompt edits it.
fields.feature_2:
Every signup in a table you own

Each signup lands as a row in a database you own, with the email and the wallet address side by side. Sort by date to see how many people joined after a given announcement.
fields.feature_3:
Alerts when a request needs a person

Say in the prompt which requests need a human, such as a redemption or a press question. The app sends an email, Slack, or in-app alert that carries the details of each one.
fields.feature_4:
Connected to the tools behind the drop

The app connects to any tool with an API. Signups can flow out to the CRM or email tool the team uses, and order details can come in from the store with no copying by hand.
fields.feature_5:
The collection's name as the address

Put the page on a custom domain such as nameofdrop.com; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. A short address reads well on a poster at a gallery show.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

The free tier covers building and publishing the page. On paid plans, Emergent exports the full code to your GitHub repository, where a developer can keep editing it.

fields.tab_content_1:
Of 1,318 signups, 47 needed a corrected wallet address

Wren Okafor opened the allowlist for Saltmarsh Studies with a form that asks for an email and a wallet address. Before a row is saved, the form checks that the address is 42 characters and starts with 0x. Of 1,318 signups, 1,271 passed on the first try and 47 were asked to fix the address.
fields.tab_content_2:
A reminder lands 1 hour ahead in each collector's time zone

Each signup on the Lumen Harbor page picks a time zone from a list. The app emails every signup 1 hour before the drop, with the start time shown in that person's own zone. The spring drop sent 2,040 reminders: 1,120 to the Americas, 610 to Europe, and 310 to Asia-Pacific.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each jacket redemption reaches Imani Castell on Slack

Every Northgate Supply collectible comes with a physical jacket. Holders enter the token number and a shipping address on the redemption form, and each request goes to fulfillment lead Imani Castell as a Slack message. In the first week 412 holders redeemed; 38 of those jackets ship outside the US.
fields.tab_content_4:
Newsletter readers made up 212 of the 464 signups

Photographer Soren Vale announced the Tidewater series in three places, each with its own link. The app saves the link each signup came from, and the table shows where people heard about the drop. Of 464 signups, 212 came from the newsletter, 158 from the community server, and 94 from social posts.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an NFT Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to build and test an NFT landing page that collects signups before the drop.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide the one thing a collector does
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Check wallet addresses on the form
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick a single action for the page: join the allowlist, set a reminder, or redeem a token. Put that form right under the artwork, and move press links and team bios further down.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Say what the work is and who made it, then say when the drop happens. Leave out price predictions and talk of future value: the page describes the work and the drop.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the sections and the form fields, and say where each signup goes and who gets an alert. Emergent builds the page and the database behind it, and a second prompt changes either one.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Have the form check each address against the format of the chain the collection uses before it saves a row. A pasted fragment then gets caught while the allowlist is still open.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Write alt text for every artwork
fields.howto_step_5_des: WCAG 2.2 criterion 1.1.1 reads: all non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose. Describe what each piece shows, such as a gull over a marsh at dusk.
fields.howto_step_6_des: The web.dev guide says sites should strive to have Largest Contentful Paint of 2.5 seconds or less. Export each piece at the width the grid shows it, then open the page on a phone over cellular data.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test the form, then share the link
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sign up from your own phone once with a correct address and once with a broken one, and check the table and the alerts. Then give the newsletter and each community its own link.

faq_plan.q: What is an NFT landing page?
faq_plan.a: An NFT landing page is a single page for one collection or drop: it shows the artwork, says when the drop happens, and asks a visitor to take one step, such as joining the allowlist. The tokens behind it follow a standard such as EIP-721, which says NFTs can represent ownership over digital or physical assets.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an NFT landing page?
faq_plan.a: Write one prompt that names the collection and the form you need, and Emergent's AI landing page builder builds the page with a table for every signup. Change the artwork or the form later with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: What should an NFT landing page template include?
faq_plan.a: It should include five parts: the artwork up front, a two-line story of the collection, the drop date with its time zone, one signup or allowlist form, and a short FAQ for collectors. Replace the template's sample art with your own pieces, and cut any section that has nothing real to say yet. Emergent builds those parts from a plain-English prompt and changes them when you prompt again.

faq_plan.q: How is an NFT landing page different from a product page?
faq_plan.a: A drop page works to a date: it builds toward one moment and collects signups before it. A product landing page sells something a visitor can buy on any day, and it leads with the item and how it ships. If the collectible comes with a physical item, keep the redemption form on the drop page for holders.

faq_plan.q: How do I collect wallet addresses on an NFT landing page?
faq_plan.a: Add a wallet address field next to the email, and have the form check its format before saving. The ethereum.org docs say an externally owned account has a 42-character address; on another chain, match that chain's format. Ask only for the public address, never a private key or recovery phrase. The app saves each address to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should the first screen of an NFT landing page show?
faq_plan.a: Show one piece of the artwork, the collection name, the date and time of the drop, and the form. A collector who reads nothing else should still know what the collection is and when it opens. Put the roadmap and the team bios below that first screen.

faq_plan.q: Should an NFT landing page focus on the artist or the collection?
faq_plan.a: Focus on the collection. A drop page has one job, getting signups before a date, and the artist's name and a short bio support that job. For a page about yourself and all of your work, with every release in one place, build an artist landing page and link to the drop from it.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep artwork from slowing down an NFT landing page?
faq_plan.a: Show a compressed preview on the page and link to the full-resolution file for collectors who want it. Set animated pieces to play only when a visitor taps them, and keep the first piece on the screen a still image.

faq_plan.q: How long before the drop should an NFT landing page go live?
faq_plan.a: Publish it once the artwork and the drop date are final. Give the allowlist at least 2 weeks to fill, post the link wherever collectors already follow the work, and send reminder emails in the last hour before the drop opens.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse an NFT landing page for the next drop?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Prompt Emergent to change the artwork and the date for the next drop, and add a column for the drop name so each drop's signups stay apart in the table. The same prompt-first approach builds pages well outside NFTs, such as a mortgage landing page.

plan.angle: The top results for this keyword are design galleries and templates (screenshots, Figma files, a paid Webflow theme); they show how an NFT page looks and stop before anything happens on it. This page shows four drop and collection pages built from a prompt and follows what happens after a collector arrives: an allowlist form that checks each wallet address is 42 characters and starts with 0x, mint-day reminders sent in each collector's time zone, a redemption form for a token that comes with a physical jacket, and a photo series page that saves which link each signup came from. No price, value or return talk anywhere: the page is about building the drop page. The FAQ covers the definition, the build, what a template should hold, a drop page versus a product page, collecting addresses, the first screen, artist versus collection focus, image weight, alt text for artwork, and reusing the structure.
